basis: 全文从年轻人不赞成总统用推特说起，指出人们开始提高媒体素养（第二段），年轻人越来越善于在网上分辨真假（第三段），社交媒体让用户更注意自己转发信息的作用，假新闻的关键在于读者是否转发（第五段），最后说年轻人在思维能力和何时在社交媒体上分享方面表现出自律。中心是网上分享新闻的辨别能力在提高。
map: more skillful / thinking skills … when to share
A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online

wrong.text: 批评总统发推太多只是开头和结尾的例子，不是全文中心。
“分布式信任”是核实新闻的方法，原文没说社交媒体上互信在积累。
转发新闻表达个人价值观和兴趣只是第五段的一句话。

context.text: … It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 ==on the basis of a vague agreement which **took far too little account of the patients’ rights**== and their expectations of privacy.

questions.stem: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?

options.A: It caused conflicts among tech giants.
options.B: It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.
options.C: It fell short of the latter’s expectations.
options.D: It put both sides into a dangerous situation.

questions.answerZh: 它未能对患者权利给予应有的关注
basis: 第一段末：信息专员德纳姆对皇家自由医院信托作出严厉裁决，因为它在 2015 年依据一份模糊的协议，把 160 万名患者的病历交给了 DeepMind，而这份协议对患者的权利和隐私期望考虑得太少（took far too little account of）。也就是没有充分重视患者的权利。
map: took far too little account of the patients’ rights
It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.

wrong.text: 原文说可能让权力进一步集中到科技巨头手中，不是在科技巨头之间引发冲突。
协议没顾及的是患者的期望，不是 DeepMind 的期望。
原文说要先承认双方本意是好的，没说协议让双方陷入危险。

context.text: DeepMind has almost apologized. ==The NHS trust has **mended its ways**==. Further arrangements —and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind ==will be **carefully scrutinised**== to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. …

questions.stem: The NHS trust responded to Denham’s verdict with ______.

options.C: necessary adjustments
options.D: sincere apologies

questions.answerZh: 必要的调整
basis: 第二段：DeepMind 差不多已经道歉，NHS 的这个信托已经改正了做法（mended its ways）。今后双方的合作都会受到仔细审查，确保征得患者的必要许可，删除不必要的数据。信托对裁决的回应是作出必要的调整。
map: has mended its ways
necessary adjustments

wrong.text: 信托已经改正了做法，不是空口许诺。
信托接受了裁决并改正，没有强硬抵制。
差不多道了歉的是 DeepMind，不是 NHS 信托。

context.text: … But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it “controlled” the data and DeepMind merely “processed” it. But this distinction misses the point that ==it is **processing and aggregation**, not the mere possession of bits, that **gives the data value**==.

questions.stem: The author argues in Paragraph 2 that ______.

options.A: privacy protection must be secured at all costs
options.B: leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it
options.C: making profits from patients’ data is illegal
options.D: the value of data comes from the processing of it

questions.answerZh: 数据的价值来自于对它的处理
basis: 第二段后半：隐私不是本案唯一的角度，甚至不是最重要的。德纳姆把责任集中在 NHS 信托上，因为按现行法律，信托“控制”数据，DeepMind 只是“处理”数据。作者认为这种区分没有抓住要点：让数据有价值的，是处理和汇总数据，而不是单纯拥有数据。
map: processing and aggregation … gives the data value
the value of data comes from the processing of it

wrong.text: 作者说隐私不是唯一的角度，甚至不是最重要的。
原文没有比较泄露和出售患者数据。
原文没说用患者数据赚钱是违法的。

context.text: … ==This practice does not address **the real worry**==. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that ==they will belong to **a private monopoly** which developed them using public resources==. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed ==to avoid a future of **digital feudalism**==. …

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is ______.

options.A: the vicious rivalry among big pharmas
options.B: the ineffective enforcement of privacy law
options.C: the uncontrolled use of new software
options.D: the monopoly of big data by tech giants

questions.answerZh: 科技巨头对大数据的垄断
basis: 最后一段：用隐私法约束科技巨头不太对路，解决不了真正的担忧（the real worry）。重要的是，DeepMind 开发的算法将属于一家私人垄断企业，而它是用公共资源开发出来的；作者还警告要避免“数字封建主义”的未来。真正的担忧是科技巨头垄断大数据。
map: belong to a private monopoly / digital feudalism
the monopoly of big data by tech giants

wrong.text: big pharma 只是类比，说大数据可能像大药企那样行事，不是说药企之间恶性竞争。
作者说用隐私法约束科技巨头不太对路，不是说隐私法执行不力。
作者担心的是算法被私人垄断，不是新软件被滥用。

context.text: … ==The potential of this work applied to healthcare is **very great**, but it could also lead to **further concentration of power** in the tech giants==. …
… We are still at the beginning of this revolution and ==small choices now may turn out to have **gigantic consequences** later==. …

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward the application of AI to healthcare is ______.

options.C: appreciative
options.D: contemptuous

questions.answerZh: 谨慎的
basis: 第一段：人工智能用于医疗潜力很大，但也可能让权力进一步集中到科技巨头手中。最后一段：这场革命才刚开始，现在的小选择以后可能产生巨大后果，要经过长期斗争才能避免数字封建主义。作者既看到好处，也提醒风险，态度是谨慎的。
map: very great, but … / small choices … gigantic consequences
cautious

wrong.text: 作者立场很清楚：肯定潜力，也警惕垄断，并不含糊。
作者只在开头肯定了潜力，全文重点在提醒风险。
作者承认潜力巨大，没有轻视。

context.text: … Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and ==a regulatory structure that **denies management the flexibility** to adjust its operations to the new reality==.

questions.stem: The financial problem with the USPS is caused partly by ______.

options.C: the cost for technical upgrading
options.D: the withdrawal of bank support

questions.answerZh: 其僵化的管理
basis: 第一段末：从根本上说，美国邮政夹在两者之间：一是技术变化永久减少了对其主打产品一类邮件的需求，二是监管体制不给管理层灵活调整经营、适应新现实的余地（denies management the flexibility）。管理缺乏灵活性，就是管理僵化。
map: denies management the flexibility
its rigid management

wrong.text: 连续多年支出大于收入是财务问题本身，不是造成问题的原因。
原文说技术变化减少了对一类邮件的需求，没说技术升级花了很多钱。
原文没提银行停止支持。

context.text: And ==interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers **exert self-interested pressure**== on the USPS’s ultimate overseer—Congress—insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. ==**This is why** repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed== in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills ==except by **deferring vital modernization**==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the USPS fails to modernize itself due to ______.

options.C: the shrinking demand for postal service
options.D: the incompetence of postal unions

questions.answerZh: 利益集团的干预
basis: 第二段：从邮政工会到贺卡制造商的各种利益集团，出于私利向国会施压，坚持要保护它们依赖的现状。这就是（This is why）近年来改革立法屡屡失败的原因，结果邮政只能靠推迟至关重要的现代化来支付账单。无法现代化是因为利益集团的干预。
map: exert self-interested pressure … This is why
the interference from interest groups

wrong.text: 原文说利益集团向国会施压，没说国会拨款不足。
需求萎缩是第一段讲的财务困境原因，不是第二段说的无法现代化的原因。
邮政工会只是利益集团之一，原文也没说它无能。

context.text: … Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. ==The latter step would largely **offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care**, thus **addressing a long-standing complaint**== by the USPS and its unions.

questions.stem: The long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions can be addressed by ______.

options.A: removing its burden of retiree health care
options.B: making more investment in new vehicles
options.C: adopting a new rate-increase mechanism
options.D: attracting more first-class mail users

questions.answerZh: 减轻其退休人员医疗保健的负担
basis: 第三段：省下的钱主要来自两处，一是每封信永久涨价一美分，二是把邮政退休人员转入联邦医疗保险（Medicare）。后一项能大大抵消每年预先支付退休人员医保的财务负担，从而解决（addressing）美国邮政及其工会长期以来的抱怨。
map: offset the financial burden of … retiree health care
removing its burden of retiree health care

wrong.text: 买新车是省下的钱的用途之一，与长期抱怨无关。
涨价是钱的另一个来源，解决长期抱怨的是后一项措施。
原文没说要吸引更多一类邮件用户。

context.text: … The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that ==legislators are **getting frightened** about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse== at the USPS. ==It is not, however, a sign that they’re **getting serious** about transforming the postal system== for the 21st century.

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author seems to view legislators with ______.

options.C: discontent
options.D: gratitude

questions.answerZh: 不满
basis: 最后一段末：围绕法案形成的共识，说明立法者害怕邮政在短期内崩溃让他们在政治上难堪；然而这并不说明他们开始认真考虑让邮政系统面向 21 世纪转型。只顾眼前、不想长远，作者对立法者是不满的。
map: It is not, however, a sign that they’re getting serious
discontent

wrong.text: 作者批评立法者只怕难堪、不认真改革，谈不上尊重。
作者对立法者的做法是批评，不是宽容。
作者没有感激立法者。

context.text: If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate—where someone is bound to point out that ==it amounts to the **bare, bare minimum** necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, **not comprehensive reform**==. …

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.A: The USPS Starts to Miss Its Good Old Days
options.B: The Postal Service: Keep Away from My Cheese
options.C: The USPS: Chronic Illness Requires a Quick Cure
options.D: The Postal Service Needs More Than a Band-Aid

questions.answerZh: 邮政服务需要的不仅仅是创可贴
basis: 全文先说美国邮政连年亏损、濒临破产，根源在需求下降和僵化的监管；利益集团阻挠改革。现在各方终于就法案达成一致，但最后一段说它只是让邮政勉强维持下去的最低限度措施，不是全面改革。Band-Aid（创可贴）比喻权宜之计，邮政需要的不只是创可贴，而是真正的改革。
map: the bare, bare minimum … not comprehensive reform
The Postal Service Needs More Than a Band-Aid

wrong.text: 原文没说邮政怀念过去的好日子。
利益集团保护自己的“奶酪”只是第二段的内容，不是全文中心。
作者批评的正是眼下的快速补救，主张全面改革，不是要快速治疗。

context.text: Americans are ==willing to **tolerate time-consuming security procedures** in return for increased safety==. The crash of EgyptAir Flight 804, which terrorists may have downed over the Mediterranean Sea, ==provides **another tragic reminder of why**==. …

questions.stem: The crash of EgyptAir Flight 804 is mentioned to ______.

options.A: stress the urgency to strengthen security worldwide
options.B: explain American’s tolerance of current security checks
options.C: highlight the necessity of upgrading major U.S. airports
options.D: emphasize the importance of privacy protection

questions.answerZh: 解释美国人对当前安检的容忍
basis: 第二段：美国人愿意忍受费时的安检程序（tolerate time-consuming security procedures）来换取更高的安全。埃及航空 804 航班可能被恐怖分子击落，这场悲剧再次提醒人们为什么（another tragic reminder of why）。why 承接上句，空难的例子是用来解释美国人为什么能容忍现行的安检。
map: tolerate time-consuming security procedures / reminder of why
explain American’s tolerance of current security checks

wrong.text: 空难说明的是航空旅行的安全风险，原文没有上升到加强全球安全，更没有呼吁其紧迫性。
第五段说预检计划不需要改造机场，针对的是安检费时，与空难无关。
第二段末的 private lives 指浪费时间拖累私人生活，与隐私保护无关。

context.text: … Enhanced security measures since then, ==combined with **a rise in airline travel**== due to the improving economy and low oil prices, ==**have resulted in** long waits at major airports== such as Chicago’s O’Hare International. …

questions.stem: Which of the following contributes to long waits at major airports?

options.B: The declining efficiency of the TSA.
options.C: An increase in the number of travelers.
options.D: Frequent unexpected secret checks.

questions.answerZh: 旅客数量的增加
basis: 第三段：自那以后加强的安全措施，加上经济好转、油价低带来的航空出行增加（a rise in airline travel），导致（have resulted in）主要机场等候时间过长。题干的 contributes to long waits 对应 have resulted in long waits，航空出行增加就是旅客数量增加。
map: a rise in airline travel
An increase in the number of travelers.

wrong.text: 第四段说的是乘客把随身行李塞得太多，不是对随身行李有新限制。
第四段说 TSA 没料到客流激增，正在赶招安检员，不是说它效率在下降。
第三段只提到去年的一次秘密调查，不是频繁的突击调查。

context.text: … Passengers who pass a background check are ==eligible to use **expedited** screening lanes==. This allows the TSA to focus on travelers who are higher risk, ==**saving time** for everyone involved==. …

questions.stem: The word “expedited” (Para. 5) is closest in meaning to ______.

options.C: wider
options.D: cheaper

questions.answerZh: 更快的
basis: 第五段：通过背景调查的乘客可以使用 expedited 安检通道，这样 TSA 能集中检查高风险旅客，为所有相关的人节省时间（saving time）。可见 expedited 与“节省时间”有关，意思是加快的，与 faster 最接近。
map: expedited / saving time
faster

wrong.text: 通道安静与否和节省时间无关，原文没有涉及。
第四段说机场空间有限、安检通道数量不够，不是通道不够宽。
第六段说的贵是加入预检计划要交的费用，不是使用安检通道要收费。

context.text: It has not gotten anywhere close to that, and ==one big reason is **sticker shock**==: Passengers must pay $85 every five years to process their background checks. Since the beginning, ==this price tag has been PreCheck’s **fatal flaw**==. Upcoming reforms might ==bring the price to a **more reasonable level**==. …

questions.stem: One problem with the PreCheck program is ______.

options.A: a dramatic reduction of its scale
options.C: the government’s reluctance to back it
options.D: an unreasonable price for enrollment

questions.answerZh: 不合理的注册价格
basis: 第六段：预检计划远没达到 2500 万人的目标，一大原因是 sticker shock（标价高得吓人）：乘客每五年要交 85 美元做背景调查。这个价格从一开始就是预检计划的致命缺陷（fatal flaw），即将进行的改革可能把价格降到更合理的水平（more reasonable level）。问题在于加入费用不合理。
map: sticker shock / price tag … fatal flaw
an unreasonable price for enrollment

wrong.text: 原文说参加人数远未达到目标，计划从一开始就有缺陷，不是规模由大变小。
原文说的是价格过高，没说计划的实施方向错了。
作者建议国会直接出钱降价，是嫌它做得不够直接，不是说政府不愿支持。

context.text: … at least at some major U.S. airports with ==increasingly **massive security lines**==.
The TSA cannot continue diverting resources into underused PreCheck lanes while ==most of the traveling public **suffers in unnecessary lines**==. It is long past time to make the program work.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.C: Less Screening for More Safety
options.D: Underused PreCheck Lanes

questions.answerZh: 被困在安检队伍中
basis: 首段提出问题：一些美国大机场安检队伍越来越长，要提前三小时到机场。第二段讲浪费时间的害处，第三、四段分析排长队的原因，第五到七段提出办法：让更多人加入预检计划。末段又说大多数旅客在不必要的队伍里受苦。全文围绕旅客被困在安检长队里这个问题展开。
map: massive security lines / suffers in unnecessary lines
Getting Stuck in Security Lines

wrong.text: 末段 long past time 是说早该让预检计划发挥作用，计划本来就有，不是来得太晚。
全文讨论的是安检耗时，不是怎样少安检、多安全。
预检通道利用不足只是第七段的内容，属于解决办法部分，概括不了全文。

context.text: ==“The ancient Hawaiians **were astronomers**,”== wrote Queen Liliuokalani, Hawaii’s last reigning monarch, in 1897. ==Star watchers were among **the most esteemed members** of Hawaiian society==. …

questions.stem: Queen Liliuokalani’s remark in Paragraph 1 indicates ______.

options.A: her conservative view on the historical role of astronomy
options.B: the importance of astronomy in ancient Hawaiian society
options.C: the regrettable decline of astronomy in ancient times
options.D: her appreciation of star watchers’ feats in her time

questions.answerZh: 天文学在古代夏威夷社会中的重要性
basis: 第一段：女王说“古代夏威夷人都是天文学家”，下一句解释观星者是夏威夷社会最受尊敬的成员之一（the most esteemed members）。观星者受尊敬，说明天文学在古代夏威夷社会很重要。
map: the most esteemed members of Hawaiian society
the importance of astronomy in ancient Hawaiian society

wrong.text: 女王对古代天文学的地位是充分肯定的，谈不上保守。
天文学处境不好说的是今天的夏威夷（Sadly … today），不是古代。
原文只说观星者受尊敬，没说女王赞赏她那个时代观星者的功绩；女王说的是古代。

context.text: … But Mauna Kea is also home to some of the world’s most powerful telescopes. Rested in the Pacific Ocean, ==Mauna Kea’s peak **rises above the bulk of our planet’s dense atmosphere**==, where conditions allow telescopes to obtain ==images of **unsurpassed clarity**==.

questions.stem: Mauna Kea is deemed as an ideal astronomical site due to ______.

options.C: its religious implications
options.D: its existing infrastructure

questions.answerZh: 其地理特征
basis: 第二段：莫纳克亚山上有世界上一些最强大的望远镜。它位于太平洋中，山顶高出地球稠密大气层的大部分（rises above the bulk of our planet’s dense atmosphere），那里的条件能让望远镜拍到无比清晰的图像（unsurpassed clarity）。它适合天文观测，是因为它的地理特征。
map: peak rises above the bulk of our planet’s dense atmosphere
its geographical features

wrong.text: 位于太平洋中只是交代位置，原文没说四面环海能起保护作用。
宗教意义是一些夏威夷人反对建望远镜的原因，不是它适合天文观测的原因。
山上已有很多望远镜是它条件理想的结果，不是原因。

context.text: Opposition to telescopes on Mauna Kea is nothing new. A small but vocal group of Hawaiians and environmentalists have long viewed their presence as disrespect for sacred land and ==**a painful reminder** of the **occupation** of what was once a sovereign nation==.

questions.stem: The construction of the TMT is opposed by some locals partly because ______.

options.A: it may risk ruining their intellectual life
options.B: it reminds them of a humiliating history
options.C: their culture will lose a chance of revival
options.D: they fear losing control of Mauna Kea

questions.answerZh: 它让他们想起一段屈辱的历史
basis: 第三段：反对在莫纳克亚山上建望远镜由来已久。一小群直言不讳的夏威夷人和环保人士一直认为，这些望远镜是对圣地的不敬，也让人痛苦地想起（a painful reminder）这个曾经的主权国家被占领（occupation）的历史。也就是让他们想起屈辱的历史。
map: a painful reminder of the occupation
it reminds them of a humiliating history

wrong.text: 原文说望远镜是对圣地的不敬，涉及宗教信仰，不是破坏他们的智识生活。
第四段说夏威夷文化正在复兴，没说会失去复兴的机会。
原文说的是历史上被占领，没说当地人怕失去对这座山的控制。

context.text: Yet science has a cultural history, too, with roots going back to the dawn of civilization. ==**The same curiosity** to find what lies beyond the horizon== that first brought early Polynesians to Hawaii’s shores inspires astronomers today to explore the heavens. Calls to disassemble all telescopes on Mauna Kea or to ban future development there ignore the reality that astronomy and Hawaiian culture ==**both seek to answer big questions**== about who we are, where we come from and where we are going. Perhaps that is why we explore the starry skies, as if answering a primal calling to ==know ourselves and our **true ancestral homes**==.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 5 that progress in today’s astronomy ______.

options.A: is fulfilling the dreams of ancient Hawaiians
options.B: helps spread Hawaiian culture across the world
options.C: may uncover the origin of Hawaiian culture
options.D: will eventually soften Hawaiians’ hostility

questions.answerZh: 正在实现古代夏威夷人的梦想
basis: 第五段：科学也有文化历史。当年把波利尼西亚人带到夏威夷的好奇心（The same curiosity），今天也激励天文学家探索星空；天文学和夏威夷文化都想回答我们是谁、从哪里来、到哪里去这些大问题（both seek to answer big questions），就像在回应了解自己和祖先真正家园的原始召唤。天文学的进步是在实现古代夏威夷人的梦想。
map: The same curiosity / both seek to answer big questions
is fulfilling the dreams of ancient Hawaiians

wrong.text: 好奇心把早期波利尼西亚人带到夏威夷，说的是两者相通，原文没说天文学帮助传播夏威夷文化。
where we come from 是天文学和夏威夷文化共同追问的问题，不是说天文学会揭示夏威夷文化的起源。
缓和敌意也许是作者的期望，原文没有这样说。

context.text: … ==**Sadly**, all is not well with astronomy in Hawaii today==. …
… ==There is **no reason why everyone cannot be welcomed** on Mauna Kea== to embrace their cultural heritage and to study the stars.

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward choosing Mauna Kea as the TMT site is one of ______.

options.C: slight hesitancy
options.D: full approval

questions.answerZh: 完全赞同
basis: 第一段用 Sadly 说天文学在夏威夷处境不好，流露出遗憾；第五段说呼吁拆除望远镜的人无视了天文学和夏威夷文化相通的现实；末段说天文学界已经在让步，完全有理由欢迎所有人到莫纳克亚山上去（There is no reason why everyone cannot be welcomed）。作者完全支持在这里建 TMT。
map: Sadly / no reason why everyone cannot be welcomed
full approval

wrong.text: 强烈反对的是第三、四段的抗议者，不是作者。
作者主动为天文学辩护，说完全有理由欢迎大家上山，不是无奈接受。
作者态度明确，没有犹豫。

context.text: Robert F. Kennedy once said that a country’s GDP measures ==“**everything except that which makes life worthwhile**.”== With Britain voting to leave the European Union, and GDP already predicted to slow as a result, it is now a timely moment to assess what he was referring to.

questions.stem: Robert F. Kennedy is cited because he ______.

options.A: praised the UK for its GDP
options.C: misinterpreted the role of GDP
options.D: had a low opinion of GDP

questions.answerZh: 对国内生产总值评价很低
basis: 第一段：肯尼迪说 GDP 能衡量“一切，除了那些让人生有价值的东西”（everything except that which makes life worthwhile）。这是说 GDP 有很大缺陷。接着作者说，英国投票脱欧、GDP 预计放缓，现在正好评估一下他的话。引用他是因为他对 GDP 评价不高。
map: everything except that which makes life worthwhile
had a low opinion of GDP

wrong.text: 英国 GDP 令西方羡慕是第二段的最新数据，不是肯尼迪的话，他也没有称赞英国。
肯尼迪说 GDP 衡量不了让人生有价值的东西，正是说 GDP 不等于幸福。
作者赞同肯尼迪的看法，并没有说他误解了 GDP。

context.text: … By most recent measures, ==the UK’s GDP has been **the envy of the Western world**==, with record low unemployment and high growth figures. If everything was going so well, then ==why did **over 17 million people vote for Brexit**==, despite the warnings about what it could do to their country’s economic prospects?

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 2 that ______.

options.A: the UK is reluctant to remold its economic pattern
options.B: GDP as the measure of success is widely defied in the UK
options.C: the UK will contribute less to the world economy
options.D: policymakers in the UK are paying less attention to GDP

questions.answerZh: 国内生产总值作为成功的衡量标准在英国被广泛反对
basis: 第二段：按最新数据，英国的 GDP 让西方世界羡慕（the envy of the Western world），失业率创新低、增长数字高。作者接着反问：既然一切都这么好，为什么还有 1700 多万人不顾对经济前景的警告投票脱欧（over 17 million people vote for Brexit）？可见很多英国人并不认同用 GDP 衡量成功。
map: the envy of the Western world … why did over 17 million people vote for Brexit
GDP as the measure of success is widely defied in the UK

wrong.text: 从 GDP 令人羡慕推不出英国不愿改变经济模式；1700 多万人投票脱欧反而说明他们想要改变。
原文只说有警告称脱欧可能（could）影响经济前景，没有断定英国对世界经济的贡献会减少。
原文说 GDP 问题困扰政策制定者半个多世纪，没说他们现在越来越不关注 GDP。

context.text: A recent annual study of countries and their ability to convert growth into well-being ==**sheds some light** on that question==. …
==This is **a lesson** that rich countries can learn==: When GDP is no longer regarded as the sole measure of a country’s success, the world looks very different.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the recent annual study?

options.B: It excludes GDP as an indicator.
options.C: Its criteria are questionable.
options.D: Its results are enlightening.

questions.answerZh: 其结果具有启发性
basis: 第三段：一项最新的年度研究考察各国把增长转化为福祉的能力，它为上段的问题提供了一些解释（sheds some light）：在 163 个国家中，英国是把经济增长转化为民生改善做得最差的之一。第四段对比富国和较穷国家，第五段说这是富国可以学到的一课（a lesson）。研究结果具有启发性。
map: sheds some light / a lesson that rich countries can learn
Its results are enlightening.

wrong.text: 163 个国家是研究衡量的对象，不是研究的发起者。
Rather than just focusing on GDP 是说不只看 GDP，还看 40 多套标准，并没有把 GDP 排除在外。
作者认为用多套标准能更全面地评估，是肯定这项研究，没有质疑其标准。

context.text: So, what Kennedy was referring to was that while GDP has been the most common method for measuring the economic activity of nations, ==as a measure, it is **no longer enough**==. ==It does not include **important factors**== such as environmental quality or education outcomes—all things that contribute to a person’s sense of well-being.
… But policymakers who ==refocus efforts on improving well-being **rather than simply worrying about GDP figures**== could avoid the forecasted doom and may even see progress.

questions.stem: In the last two paragraphs, the author suggests that ______.

options.A: the UK is preparing for an economic boom
options.B: high GDP foreshadows an economic decline
options.C: it is essential to consider factors beyond GDP
options.D: it requires caution to handle economic issues

questions.answerZh: 考虑国内生产总值以外的因素至关重要
basis: 第六段：GDP 作为衡量标准已经不够了（no longer enough），它不包括环境质量、教育成果这些关系到幸福感的重要因素。第七段：政策制定者如果把精力转向提高福祉，而不是只担心 GDP 数字（rather than simply worrying about GDP figures），就能避免预测中的厄运。作者的意思是：考虑 GDP 以外的因素非常重要。
map: no longer enough / rather than simply worrying about GDP figures
it is essential to consider factors beyond GDP

wrong.text: 第七段说全世界和英国的增长预计会受到重创，不是英国在准备经济腾飞。
decline 指增长受打击导致日常服务下降，原文没说高 GDP 预示经济衰退。
作者主张转向提高福祉、不只盯着 GDP，不是说处理经济问题要谨慎。

context.text: … Across the 163 countries measured, ==the UK is **one of the poorest performers**== in ensuring that economic growth is translated into meaningful improvements for its citizens. …
This is a lesson that rich countries can learn: ==When GDP is **no longer regarded as the sole measure** of a country’s success==, the world looks very different.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best title for the text?

options.A: High GDP But Inadequate Well-being, a UK Lesson
options.B: GDP Figures, a Window on Global Economic Health
options.C: Robert F. Kennedy, a Terminator of GDP
options.D: Brexit, the UK’s Gateway to Well-being

questions.answerZh: 高国内生产总值但福祉不足：英国的一课
basis: 前两段引肯尼迪的话质疑 GDP，并以英国 GDP 亮眼却有 1700 多万人投票脱欧为例；第三到五段用最新研究说明英国把增长转化为民生福祉做得最差之一（one of the poorest performers），这是富国可以学到的一课；最后两段说 GDP 衡量不了幸福感，政策应转向提高福祉。全文以英国为例，说明 GDP 高不等于福祉好。
map: one of the poorest performers / no longer regarded as the sole measure
High GDP But Inadequate Well-being, a UK Lesson

wrong.text: 文章说 GDP 不足以衡量国家的状况，不是把它当作观察经济健康的窗口。
肯尼迪只是批评 GDP，谈不上终结 GDP；他也不是全文的主题。
脱欧只是讨论 GDP 缺陷的切入点，原文没说脱欧是英国通往幸福之路。

context.text: … ==But it did so while **holding its nose** at the ethics of his conduct==, which included accepting gifts such as a Rolex watch and a Ferrari automobile from a company seeking access to government.
The court did suggest that accepting favors in return for opening doors ==is **“distasteful”** and “nasty.”== …

questions.stem: The underlined sentence (Para. 1) most probably shows that the court ______.

options.A: avoided defining the extent of McDonnell’s duties
options.B: made no compromise in convicting McDonnell
options.C: was contemptuous of McDonnell’s conduct
options.D: refused to comment on McDonnell’s ethics

questions.answerZh: 对麦克唐纳的行为表示蔑视
basis: 第一段：最高法院罕见地一致推翻了麦克唐纳的贪腐定罪，但（But）在这样做的同时，对他行为的道德问题捂着鼻子（holding its nose），他收了一家想接近政府的公司送的劳力士手表和法拉利。捂鼻子表示嫌恶；第四段法院也说拿好处换门路“令人反感”“下作”（distasteful, nasty）。法院对麦克唐纳的行为是蔑视的。
map: holding its nose at the ethics of his conduct
was contemptuous of McDonnell’s conduct

wrong.text: 第二段说的是初审法官没告诉陪审团只能看公务行为，不是最高法院回避界定他的职责。
最高法院推翻了对他的定罪，不是在定罪上毫不让步。
holding its nose 表示嫌恶，不是拒绝评论；第四段法院明确说了这种行为令人反感。

context.text: … But under anti-bribery laws, ==proof must be made of **concrete benefits**==, such as approval of a contract or regulation. Simply arranging a meeting, making a phone call, or hosting an event ==is **not an “official act”**==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, an official act is deemed corruptive only if it involves ______.

options.B: sizable gains in the form of gifts
options.C: concrete returns for gift-givers
options.D: breaking contracts officially

questions.answerZh: 给送礼者具体的回报
basis: 第四段：法院说拿好处换门路令人反感，但（But）根据反贿赂法，必须证明有实实在在的好处（concrete benefits），比如批准一项合同或规定；只是安排见面、打电话、举办活动，不算“公务行为”。公务行为算腐败的条件，是为送礼者提供了具体的回报。
map: proof must be made of concrete benefits
concrete returns for gift-givers

wrong.text: 第三段的 clear intent 是向官员施压的明确意图，原文没提泄密。
concrete benefits 是官员给送礼者的实际好处，不是官员自己收到的贵重礼物。
批准合同只是举例说明什么算实际好处，与违反合同无关。

context.text: … Elected leaders must be allowed to help supporters deal with bureaucratic problems without fear of prosecution for bribery. “The basic compact underlying representative government,” wrote Chief Justice John Roberts for the court, “==assumes that public officials will **hear from their constituents** and **act on their concerns**==.”

questions.stem: The court’s ruling is based on the assumption that public officials are ______.

options.A: justified in addressing the needs of their constituents
options.B: qualified to deal independently with bureaucratic issues
options.C: allowed to focus on the concerns of their supporters
options.D: exempt from conviction on the charge of favoritism

questions.answerZh: 在满足选民需求方面是正当的
basis: 第五段：法院的裁决在法律上是合理的，它界定了一种不算犯罪的偏袒：民选领导人必须能帮支持者处理官僚问题，而不必担心被控受贿。首席大法官罗伯茨写道，代议制政府的基本契约“假定公职人员会倾听选民的意见，并根据他们的关切行事”（hear from their constituents and act on their concerns）。公职人员满足选民的需求是正当的。
map: hear from their constituents and act on their concerns
justified in addressing the needs of their constituents

wrong.text: 原文说应允许他们帮支持者处理官僚问题，不是说他们有能力独立处理政府事务。
原文的假定是倾听选民并为其关切行事，不是允许官员把精力集中在支持者关心的事上。
裁决只界定了一种不算犯罪的偏袒，不是说偏袒都能免于定罪。

context.text: But the ruling reinforces the need for citizens and their elected representatives, not the courts, ==to ensure **equality of access** to government==. Officials must not be allowed to play favorites in providing information or in arranging meetings simply because an individual or group provides a campaign donation or a personal gift. ==**This type of integrity** requires well-enforced laws in government transparency==, such as records of official meetings, rules on lobbying, and information about each elected leader’s source of wealth.

questions.stem: Well-enforced laws in government transparency are needed to ______.

options.B: guarantee fair play in official access
options.C: allow for certain kinds of lobbying
options.D: inspire hopes in average people

questions.answerZh: 保证接触官员机会上的公平
basis: 第六段：裁决更说明需要由公民和他们选出的代表来保证人人都有平等的机会接触政府（equality of access）；官员不能因为谁捐了竞选资金或送了礼，就在提供信息、安排会面上偏袒谁。这种廉正（This type of integrity）需要严格执行的政府透明法律。所以这些法律是为了保证接触官员的机会公平。
map: equality of access to government / This type of integrity
guarantee fair play in official access

wrong.text: This type of integrity 指在接触政府机会上一视同仁，不是唤醒官员的良知。
rules on lobbying 是对游说的规定，目的是约束，不是给某些游说留余地。
average people 出自第七段讲双重标准的句子，原文没说要给普通人带来希望。

context.text: ==The court’s ruling is **legally sound**== in defining a kind of favoritism that is not criminal. …
The court’s ruling is ==**a step forward**== in the struggle against both corruption and official favoritism.

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward the court’s ruling is ______.

options.C: skeptical
options.D: supportive

questions.answerZh: 支持的
basis: 第五段：作者说裁决在法律上是合理的（legally sound），界定了一种不算犯罪的偏袒。第六段：裁决更强调了要保证人人平等地接触政府。第七段说偏袒不一定是腐败，但官员要避免双重标准。最后一段：这项裁决是反腐败、反公务偏袒斗争中的一大进步（a step forward）。作者支持这项裁决。
map: legally sound / a step forward
supportive

wrong.text: holding its nose 是法院对麦克唐纳行为的嫌恶，不是作者对裁决的讽刺。
作者用 legally sound、a step forward 积极肯定裁决，不只是容忍。
作者说偏袒不一定是腐败，赞同裁决，没有怀疑。

context.text: France, which prides itself as the global innovator of fashion, has decided its fashion industry ==has lost an absolute right to **define physical beauty** for women==. Its lawmakers gave preliminary approval last week to a law that would ==**make it a crime** to employ ultra-thin models on runways==. …

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, what would happen in France?

options.C: Websites about dieting would thrive.
options.D: The fashion industry would decline.

questions.answerZh: 身体美将被重新定义
basis: 第一段：法国认定其时尚业已经失去了界定女性形体美的绝对权力（lost an absolute right to define physical beauty），立法机构初步批准了一项法律，雇用极瘦模特走T台将构成犯罪；议会还同意取缔鼓吹极端节食的网站。“以超瘦为美”的标准将被重新界定，即形体美会被重新定义。
map: lost an absolute right to define physical beauty
Physical beauty would be redefined.

wrong.text: 法律禁止的是雇用极瘦模特走T台，没说要建造新的T台。
议会要取缔鼓吹极端节食的网站，这类网站不会兴盛。
时尚业失去定义美的绝对权，不等于时尚业会衰落。

context.text: … They suggest ==beauty should not be defined by looks that end up with **impinging on health**==. That’s a start. And the ban on ultra-thin models seems to go beyond ==protecting models from **starving themselves to death**==—as some have done. …

questions.stem: The phrase “impinging on” (Para. 2) is closest in meaning to ______.

options.C: losing faith in
options.D: doing harm to

questions.answerZh: 对……造成伤害
basis: 第二段：这些措施出于几个积极的动机（uplifting motives），表明美不应由最终 impinging on 健康的外表来界定。上文说法国要叫停“以极瘦为美”，下文说禁令要保护模特免于节食致死。可见极瘦的外形对健康有害，impinging on 的意思是“对……造成伤害”。
map: end up with impinging on health / starving themselves to death
doing harm to

wrong.text: 法令否定的是极瘦的外形，说这种外形“提高健康的价值”与上下文矛盾。
外表能反映健康状况是常识，但放进原句没有否定的意思，体现不出法令的用意。
节食致死说的是禁令要保护模特，不是说人们对健康失去信心。

context.text: … In Denmark, the United States, and a few other countries, ==it is trying to **set voluntary standards** for models and fashion images== that rely more on peer pressure for enforcement.
==In contrast to France’s actions, Denmark’s fashion industry **agreed last month on rules and sanctions**== regarding age, health, and other characteristics of models. …

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the fashion industry?

options.A: The French measures have already failed.
options.B: New standards are being set in Denmark.
options.C: Models are no longer under peer pressure.
options.D: Its inherent problems are getting worse.

questions.answerZh: 丹麦正在制定新的标准
basis: 第五段：在丹麦、美国和其他几个国家，时尚业正在尝试为模特和时尚形象制定自愿标准（set voluntary standards）。第六段以丹麦为例：与法国不同，丹麦时尚业上个月就模特的年龄、健康等特征制定了规则和处罚办法，还修订了《丹麦时尚道德宪章》。丹麦正在制定新标准。
map: trying to set voluntary standards / agreed last month on rules and sanctions
New standards are being set in Denmark.

wrong.text: 第四段只说法国的措施过于依赖重罚，没说已经失败。
原文说新标准更多依靠同侪压力来执行，不是说模特不再承受同侪压力。
原文说时尚业知道自己有固有问题，并正在制定标准解决，没说问题在恶化。

context.text: In contrast to France’s actions, Denmark’s fashion industry agreed last month on ==rules and sanctions regarding age, **health**, and other characteristics of models==. The newly revised Danish Fashion Ethical Charter clearly states: “We are aware of and ==**take responsibility** for the impact the fashion industry has on body ideals==, especially on young people.” The charter’s main tool of enforcement is ==to **deny access for designers** and modeling agencies to Copenhagen Fashion Week (CFW)==, which is run by the Danish Fashion Institute. …

questions.stem: A designer is most likely to be rejected by CFW for ______.

options.A: setting a high age threshold for models
options.B: caring too much about models’ character
options.C: showing little concern for health factors
options.D: pursuing perfect physical conditions

questions.answerZh: 对健康因素几乎不关心
basis: 第六段：丹麦时尚业就模特的年龄、健康等特征制定了规则和处罚办法；《丹麦时尚道德宪章》声明要为时尚业对身材理想的影响负责（take responsibility）；宪章的主要执行手段是不让违规的设计师和模特经纪公司参加哥本哈根时装周（deny access … to CFW）。所以不关心模特健康的设计师最可能被拒之门外。
map: rules and sanctions regarding … health / deny access for designers
showing little concern for health factors

wrong.text: 原文提到年龄是规则涉及的特征之一，没说设计师为模特设了高年龄门槛，更推不出会因此被拒。
原文 characteristics of models 是模特的特征，不是模特的性格（character）。
宪章反对的是时尚业推崇的极瘦身材，physical conditions 是身体状况，与原文意思不同。

context.text: The French measures, however, ==rely too much on **severe punishment** to change a culture== that still regards beauty as skin-deep—and bone-showing. …

==Relying on **ethical persuasion** rather than law to address the misuse of **body ideals**== may be the best step. Even better would be to help elevate notions of beauty beyond the material standards of a particular industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following may be the best title of the text?

options.A: The Great Threats to the Fashion Industry
options.B: Just Another Round of Struggle for Beauty
options.C: A Dilemma for the Starving Models in France
options.D: A Challenge to the Fashion Industry’s Body Ideals

questions.answerZh: 对时尚产业身体理想的挑战
basis: 全文前四段介绍并评价法国针对时尚业“以极瘦为美”的禁令，第五、六段介绍丹麦等国用自愿标准和道德劝说来解决这个问题，最后一段比较两种做法，并建议让人们对美的认识超越某个行业的物质标准。全文讲的是各方对时尚业身材理想（body ideals）发起的挑战。
map: severe punishment / ethical persuasion … body ideals
A Challenge to the Fashion Industry’s Body Ideals

wrong.text: 受到挑战的是时尚业宣扬的审美观，不是整个时尚业面临巨大威胁。
作者支持纠正畸形审美，没有把这些举措看成又一轮求美之争。
模特节食致死只是第二段的一个细节，不是全文重点。

context.text: … While polls show Britons rate “the countryside” alongside the royal family, Shakespeare and the National Health Service (NHS) ==as what makes them proudest of their country, this has **limited political support**==.

questions.stem: Britain’s public sentiment about the countryside ______.

options.A: has brought much benefit to the NHS
options.B: didn’t start till the Shakespearean age
options.C: is fully backed by the royal family
options.D: is not well reflected in politics

questions.answerZh: 在政治中没有得到很好的体现
basis: 第一段：民调显示，英国人把“乡村”与王室、莎士比亚和国民保健服务（NHS）并列，视为最让他们为国家骄傲的东西，但这种情感得到的政治支持很有限（limited political support）。也就是说，民众对乡村的感情在政治中没有得到很好的体现。
map: this has limited political support
is not well reflected in politics

wrong.text: NHS 只是和乡村并列的骄傲之一，原文没说乡村情感给 NHS 带来好处。
提到莎士比亚是为了说明英国人多看重乡村，原文没讲这种情感从什么时候开始。
王室也只是并列项，原文没介绍王室的态度。

context.text: … ==Hill’s pressure later led to the creation of **national parks and green belts**==. They don’t make countryside any more, and ==**every year** concrete **consumes more of it**==. It needs constant guardianship.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the achievements of the National Trust are now being ______.

options.C: properly protected
options.D: largely overshadowed

questions.answerZh: 逐渐摧毁
basis: 第二段：一个世纪前希尔创立国民信托，为的是永远为所有人保护自然美景；在她的推动下，后来建立了国家公园和绿化带。但现在乡村不再增加，混凝土每年都在吞噬更多乡村（every year concrete consumes more of it）。国民信托的成果正在被逐渐破坏，every year 对应 gradually，consumes 对应 destroyed。
map: every year concrete consumes more of it
gradually destroyed

wrong.text: 乡村逐年被混凝土吞噬，成果没有得到加强。
原文说乡村需要持续的保护，这是作者的呼吁，不是成果的现状。
成果是在实实在在地被吞噬，不是被别的东西掩盖、黯然失色。

context.text: … ==Only Ukip, **sensing its chance**, has sided with those pleading for a more considered approach to using green land==. Its Campaign to Protect Rural England ==**struck terror** into many local Conservative parties==.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from Paragraph 3?

options.A: Labour is under attack for opposing development.
options.C: Ukip may gain from its support for rural conservation.
options.D: The Liberal Democrats are losing political influence.

questions.answerZh: 英国独立党可能因其对乡村保护的支持而获益
basis: 第三段：下届选举中几个大党似乎都不支持保护乡村，只有英国独立党察觉到了机会（sensing its chance），站到了主张更审慎地使用绿地的人一边；它的“保护英格兰乡村运动”让许多地方保守党胆战心惊。由“嗅到机会”可以推出，独立党可能因支持保护乡村而获益。
map: sensing its chance / struck terror into … Conservative parties
Ukip may gain from its support for rural conservation.

wrong.text: 反对开发的是地方议会，工党是要在议会反对开发的地方终止地方规划，原文也没说工党受到攻击。
保守党的规划改革甚至批准“规划外”建设，没有要放弃的意思。
自由民主党只是在乡村问题上保持沉默，原文没说它正在失去政治影响力。

context.text: … Under lobby pressure, ==George Osborne **favours rural new-build** against urban renovation and renewal==. He favours out-of-town shopping sites against high streets. ==This is not a free market but **a biased one**==. Rural towns and villages have grown and will always grow. They do so best ==where building sticks to their edges and **respects their character**==. We do not ruin urban conservation areas. ==**Why ruin rural ones?**==

questions.stem: The author holds that George Osborne’s preference ______.

options.A: reveals a strong prejudice against urban areas
options.B: shows his disregard for the character of rural areas
options.C: stresses the necessity of easing the housing crisis
options.D: highlights his firm stand against lobby pressure

questions.answerZh: 表明他对乡村地区特色的漠视
basis: 第五段：在游说压力下，奥斯本支持在乡村新建而不是城市改造翻新，支持城外购物中心而不是商业街。作者批评这不是自由市场，而是有偏向的市场；乡村城镇在建筑紧贴其边缘、尊重其特色（respects their character）时发展得最好；我们不破坏城市保护区，为什么要破坏乡村的？可见奥斯本的偏好不顾乡村地区的特色。
map: favours rural new-build … Why ruin rural ones?
shows his disregard for the character of rural areas

wrong.text: 奥斯本的偏好损害的是乡村，作者说城市保护区没有被破坏，谈不上对城市有偏见。
把“住房危机”等同于“在草地上建房”的是游说团体的说辞，不是奥斯本偏好所强调的。
原文说奥斯本是在游说压力之下才有这种偏好，不是坚决对抗游说压力。

context.text: … ==Half a century of **town and country planning** has enabled it to retain an **enviable** rural coherence==, while still permitting low-density urban living. …

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author shows his appreciation of ______.

options.A: the size of population in Britain
options.B: the enviable urban lifestyle in Britain
options.C: the town-and-country planning in Britain
options.D: the political life in today’s Britain

questions.answerZh: 英国的城乡规划
basis: 最后一段：开发应当有规划，不能放任。英国是欧洲人口第二稠密的国家，半个世纪的城乡规划（town and country planning）让它保住了令人羡慕的乡村协调格局，同时还保持了低密度的城市生活。作者欣赏的是英国的城乡规划。
map: town and country planning has enabled it to retain an enviable rural coherence
the town-and-country planning in Britain

wrong.text: 原文只是交代英国是欧洲人口第二稠密的国家，作者并没有欣赏人口规模。
令人羡慕的是乡村的协调格局（rural coherence），不是城市生活方式。
作者呼吁政治左右两派联合起来避免乡村被破坏，不是欣赏当今英国的政治生活。

context.text: … ==But **even if** you accept Friedman’s premise== and regard corporate social responsibility (CSR) policies as a waste of shareholders’ money, ==things may **not be absolutely clear-cut**==. New research suggests that ==CSR may **create monetary value** for companies==—at least when they are prosecuted for corruption.

questions.stem: The author views Milton Friedman’s statement about CSR with ______.

options.C: uncertainty
options.D: approval

questions.answerZh: 怀疑
basis: 第一段：弗里德曼说企业唯一的社会责任就是增加利润。作者接着用 But 转折：即使你接受弗里德曼的前提（even if），认为企业社会责任政策是浪费股东的钱，事情也未必那么绝对（not be absolutely clear-cut）；新研究表明企业社会责任可能为公司创造货币价值。作者对弗里德曼的说法持怀疑态度。
map: But even if … not be absolutely clear-cut
skepticism

wrong.text: tolerance 总体上是接受，而作者用 But、even if 表达的是质疑。
作者明确认为事情没那么绝对，并引用新研究来反驳，不是拿不准。
accept Friedman’s premise 是让步假设，作者并不赞同。

context.text: … First, ==consumers may take CSR spending as a “signal” that a company’s products are **of high quality**==. Second, ==customers may be **willing to buy** a company’s products== as an indirect way to donate to the good causes it helps. And third, through a more diffuse “halo effect,” whereby ==its good deeds earn it **greater consideration** from consumers and others==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, CSR helps a company by ______.

options.C: protecting it from being defamed
options.D: raising the quality of its products

questions.answerZh: 赢得消费者的信任
basis: 第二段：企业社会责任可以从三方面为公司增值：一是消费者把它看作产品质量高的“信号”；二是顾客愿意买公司的产品，间接捐助公司支持的公益事业；三是通过“光环效应”，公司的善举让它赢得消费者和其他人更多的好感（greater consideration）。三点的共同之处是赢得消费者的信任。
map: take CSR spending as a “signal” / willing to buy / greater consideration
winning trust from consumers

wrong.text: 第一段说的是公司因腐败被起诉时 CSR 能带来价值，不是防止公司做出不法行为。
原文只说善举能为公司赢得更多好感，没说能保护它免遭诋毁。
原文说消费者把 CSR 支出看作产品质量高的信号，不是 CSR 真的提高了产品质量。

context.text: The study found that, among prosecuted firms, those with the most comprehensive CSR programmes ==tended to get **more lenient penalties**==. Their analysis ruled out the possibility that it was firms’ political influence, rather than their CSR stand, that accounted for the leniency: Companies that contributed more to political campaigns ==did not receive **lower fines**==.

questions.stem: The expression “more lenient” (Para. 4) is closest in meaning to ______.

options.C: less severe
options.D: more lasting

questions.answerZh: 不那么严厉的
basis: 第四段：研究发现，在被起诉的公司中，企业社会责任项目最全面的公司往往受到 more lenient 的处罚。下一句补充说，研究排除了政治影响力的作用：为政治活动捐款更多的公司并没有得到更低的罚款（lower fines）。可见 more lenient penalties 就是较轻的处罚，more lenient 意为 less severe。
map: more lenient penalties / lower fines
less severe

wrong.text: 第二句讲的是政治影响力能否带来轻罚，不是说哪种处罚更有效。
排除政治影响力是研究方法，与处罚有没有争议无关。
“更持久”借自光环效应的扩散性，但 lenient 修饰的是处罚，与持久无关。

context.text: In all, the study concludes that ==whereas prosecutors should only evaluate a case based on its merits, they **do seem to be influenced** by a company’s record in CSR==. …

questions.stem: When prosecutors evaluate a case, a company’s CSR record ______.

options.A: has an impact on their decision
options.C: increases the chance of being penalized
options.D: constitutes part of the investigation

questions.answerZh: 对他们的决定有影响
basis: 第五段首句：研究的结论是，虽然检察官本应只根据案件本身来评判，但他们似乎确实受到了公司企业社会责任记录的影响（do seem to be influenced by）。也就是说，CSR 记录会影响检察官的决定。
map: they do seem to be influenced by a company’s record in CSR
has an impact on their decision

wrong.text: 原文只说检察官受到影响，没说 CSR 记录被当作可靠证据。
原文说 CSR 做得好的公司罚款能低约 40%，不是更容易受罚。
第三段说检察官受的是光环效应的影响，原文没说 CSR 记录是调查的一部分。

context.text: Researchers admit that ==their study does not answer the question of **how much businesses ought to spend** on CSR==. …

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of CSR, according to the last paragraph?

options.A: Its negative effects on businesses are often overlooked.
options.B: The necessary amount of companies’ spending on it is unknown.
options.C: Companies’ financial capacity for it has been overestimated.
options.D: It has brought much benefit to the banking industry.

questions.answerZh: 公司在其上的必要支出数额是未知的
basis: 最后一段首句：研究人员承认，他们的研究没有回答企业应该在企业社会责任上花多少钱（how much businesses ought to spend）。也就是说，企业在这方面的必要支出是多少，目前还不知道。
map: does not answer the question of how much businesses ought to spend
The necessary amount of companies’ spending on it is unknown.

wrong.text: 末句说的是 CSR 的好处：公司惹上官司时能少受处罚，不是负面影响被忽视。
研究只是没回答该花多少，没说企业的财力被高估。
banking on 意思是“指望”，与银行业无关。

context.text: … Nostalgia for ink on paper and the rustle of pages aside, ==there’s **plenty of incentive** to ditch print==. The infrastructure required to make a physical newspaper—printing presses, delivery trucks—==isn’t just **expensive**; it’s **excessive**== at a time when online-only competitors don’t have the same set of financial constraints. …

questions.stem: The New York Times is considering ending its print edition partly due to ______.

options.C: the complaints from its readers
options.D: the high cost of operation

questions.answerZh: 高昂的运营成本
basis: 第二段：有很多理由促使报纸放弃纸质版（plenty of incentive to ditch print）。首先，印刷机、送货卡车这些出实体报纸所需的基础设施不仅昂贵（expensive），而且在只做网络版的竞争对手没有这些财务负担的时候，已经是过度的开支（excessive）。可见部分原因是运营成本高。
map: The infrastructure … isn’t just expensive; it’s excessive
the high cost of operation

wrong.text: 原文说纸质版广告销售额仍远超网络版和手机版，而且这与停办纸质版的原因无关。
原文没提投资者施压。
原文说读者正在转向网络，没说读者有抱怨。

context.text: Overhead may be high and circulation lower, but ==rushing to eliminate its print edition **would be a mistake**==, says BuzzFeed CEO Jonah Peretti.
… “==Figuring out a way to **accelerate that transition** would make sense for them==,” he said, …
==Sometimes that’s **worth making a change** anyway==. …

questions.stem: Peretti suggests that, in face of the present situation, the Times should ______.

options.B: end the print edition for good
options.C: seek new sources of readership
options.D: aim for efficient management

questions.answerZh: 进行战略调整
basis: 第三到五段是佩雷蒂的看法：急于砍掉纸质版是个错误（would be a mistake）；《纽约时报》应抓紧退出纸质业务，但要用对方法，想办法加快转型才明智（accelerate that transition）；有时候值得做出改变，比如提价，把纸质版做成传承产品。佩雷蒂主张的是做出战略性调整。
map: accelerate that transition / worth making a change
make strategic adjustments

wrong.text: 佩雷蒂说急于砍掉纸质版是个错误，会让最忠实的读者不满。
佩雷蒂的思路是为现有最忠实的读者做纸质版，没说要寻找新读者。
报纸面临的是纸质版去留问题，不是管理效率问题。

context.text: … ==The **most loyal customers** would still get the product they favor==, the idea goes, and they’d feel like they were helping sustain the quality of something they believe in. “So if you’re overpaying for print, you could feel like you were helping,” Peretti said. “Then increase it at a higher rate each year and essentially try to generate additional revenue.” In other words, if you’re going to make a print product, ==make it for the people who are **already obsessed with it**==. …

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraphs 5 and 6 that a “legacy product” ______.

options.A: helps restore the glory of former times
options.B: is meant for the most loyal customers
options.C: will have the cost of printing reduced
options.D: expands the popularity of the paper

questions.answerZh: 是为最忠实的顾客准备的
basis: 第五段末佩雷蒂提出把纸质版提价，做成传承产品（legacy product）。第六段解释这个想法：最忠实的顾客仍能买到喜欢的产品，还会觉得自己在帮着维持所信赖的东西的品质；换句话说，要做纸质产品，就为已经痴迷于它的人来做（make it for the people who are already obsessed with it）。传承产品就是专为最忠实的顾客打造的。
map: The most loyal customers … make it for the people who are already obsessed with it
is meant for the most loyal customers

wrong.text: 原文说的是读者觉得在帮着维持（sustain）品质，不是恢复（restore）昔日辉煌。
第六段说的是提价、创造额外收入，不是降低印刷成本。
纸质版专为少数最忠实的读者而做，不是要扩大报纸的受众。

context.text: … “But we’re going to have questions like that where we have things we’re doing that don’t make sense ==when the market changes and **the world changes**==. In those situations, ==it’s better to be **more aggressive** than less aggressive==.”

questions.stem: Peretti believes that, in a changing world, ______.

options.C: aggressiveness better meets challenges
options.D: legacy businesses are becoming outdated

questions.answerZh: 进取心更能应对挑战
basis: 最后一段：佩雷蒂说，BuzzFeed 没有传统业务是一大幸事，但当市场和世界发生变化时，他们手上的事也会变得不合时宜，也会遇到类似的问题。在那种情况下，更加积极进取比不那么积极要好（better to be more aggressive）。在变化的世界里，积极进取能更好地应对挑战。
map: it’s better to be more aggressive than less aggressive
aggressiveness better meets challenges

wrong.text: 原文没讲传统奢侈品，世界在变，任何业务都可能受到冲击。
佩雷蒂主张更积极进取，不是更谨慎。
佩雷蒂建议把纸质版做成传承产品，没说传统业务正在过时。

context.text: Sometimes that’s worth making a change anyway. Peretti gives the example of Netflix discontinuing its DVD-mailing service to focus on streaming. “It was seen as a blunder,” he said. The move turned out to be foresighted. And if Peretti were in charge at the Times? “ I wouldn’t pick a year to end print,” he said. ==“I would **raise prices** and make it into more of a **legacy product**.”==
… Getting the print edition seven days a week ==costs nearly $500 a year - **more than twice as much** as a digital-only subscription==.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title of the text?

options.A: Shift to Online Newspapers All at Once
options.B: Cherish the Newspaper Still in Your Hand
options.C: Keep Your Newspapers Forever in Fashion
options.D: Make Your Print Newspaper a Luxury Good

questions.answerZh: 让你的印刷版报纸成为奢侈品
basis: 前两段交代《纽约时报》考虑放弃纸质版的背景和原因，后面几段是佩雷蒂的看法：不要急着砍掉纸质版，而是提高价格，把它做成传承产品（raise prices … legacy product），专为最忠实的读者而做；《纽约时报》纸质版一年近 500 美元，是纯电子版的两倍多。全文的建议就是把纸质报纸做成一种奢侈品。
map: raise prices and make it into more of a legacy product
Make Your Print Newspaper a Luxury Good

wrong.text: 佩雷蒂说急于砍掉纸质版是个错误，不主张立刻全面转向网络。
第二段提到对纸张的怀旧只是背景，全文是在讲应对之策，不是怀念纸质报纸。
全文讲纸质版的去留和定位，不是让报纸永远时尚，也漏了 print 这个重点。

context.text: King Juan Carlos of Spain once insisted “kings don’t abdicate, they die in their sleep.” ==But **embarrassing scandals**== and the popularity of the republican left in the recent Euro-elections have ==forced him to eat his words and **stand down**==. …

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, king Juan Carlos of Spain ______.

options.A: used to enjoy high public support
options.C: eased his relationship with his rivals
options.D: ended his reign in embarrassment

questions.answerZh: 在尴尬中结束了他的统治
basis: 第一段：卡洛斯曾坚称“国王不退位，他们在睡梦中死去”，但令人尴尬的丑闻（embarrassing scandals）和共和派左翼在欧洲选举中的人气，迫使他食言并退位（stand down）。stand down 与前句的 abdicate 同义，即退位。卡洛斯是在尴尬中结束了自己的统治。
map: embarrassing scandals … stand down
ended his reign in embarrassment

wrong.text: 原文受欢迎（popularity）的是共和派左翼，不是卡洛斯。
原文提到欧洲王室，只是说西班牙的事对他们有警示，没说卡洛斯和他们的关系。
原文说对手迫使他退位，双方关系是更紧张，不是缓和。

context.text: ==It is this apparent **transcendence of politics**== that explains monarchs’ continuing popularity as heads of state. And so, the Middle East excepted, Europe is the most monarch-infested region in the world, with 10 kingdoms (not counting Vatican city and Andorra). But unlike their absolutist counterparts in the Gulf and Asia, most royal families have survived because they allow voters to ==avoid the difficult search for a **non-controversial but respected** public figure==.

questions.stem: Monarchs are kept as heads of state in Europe mostly ______.

options.A: owing to their undoubted and respectable status
options.B: to achieve a balance between tradition and reality
options.C: to give voters more public figures to look up to
options.D: due to their everlasting political embodiment

questions.answerZh: 因为他们无可置疑、受人尊敬的地位

context.text: Americans should take steps to protect their digital privacy. context.text: The purpose of editing the News of the World ==was not to promote reader understanding, **to be fair** in what was written or to betray any **common humanity**==. ==It was to **ruin lives** in the quest for circulation and impact.== …

questions.stem: Which of the following is suggested in the last paragraph?

options.A: The quality of writings is of primary importance.
options.B: Common humanity is central to news reporting.
options.C: Moral awareness matters in editing a newspaper.
options.D: Journalists need stricter industrial regulations.

questions.answerZh: 道德意识在编辑报纸时很重要
basis: 末段：编辑《世界新闻报》的目的不是增进读者理解、公正报道（to be fair）或展现共同的人性（common humanity），而是为了追求发行量和影响力去毁掉别人的生活（ruin lives）。作者通过批评这种做法，从反面强调道德意识对编辑报纸很重要。
map: not … to be fair … or to betray any common humanity / to ruin lives
Moral awareness matters in editing a newspaper.

wrong.text: 增进读者理解是编报的基本职责，原文没谈写作质量。
展现共同人性只是原文提到的目的之一，选项说成新闻报道的核心。
作者从道德层面批评，没提出要制定更严格的行业规定。

context.text: In order to “change lives for the better” and ==reduce “**dependency**”==, George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, introduced the “upfront work search” scheme. Only if the jobless arrive at the jobcentre with a CV, register for online job search, and ==**start looking for work** will they be **eligible for benefit**==—and then they should report weekly rather than fortnightly. What could be more reasonable?

questions.stem: George Osborne’s scheme was intended to _______.

options.A: motivate the unemployed to report voluntarily
options.B: provide the unemployed with easier access to benefits
options.C: encourage jobseekers’ active engagement in job seeking
options.D: guarantee jobseekers’ legitimate right to benefits

questions.answerZh: 鼓励求职者积极参与求职
basis: 第一段：奥斯本推出“预先求职”方案，目的是“让生活更好”、减少“依赖”（reduce “dependency”）。具体规定是：失业者只有带简历到就业中心、在网上注册求职、并开始找工作（start looking for work），才有资格领取救济金，之后还要每周报到。结合目的和规定可知，方案是要鼓励求职者积极找工作，而不是依赖救济金。
map: start looking for work … reduce “dependency”
encourage jobseekers’ active engagement in job seeking

wrong.text: 每周报到只是方案的细节，而且是强制规定（they should report），不是鼓励自愿报告。
方案给领取救济金设了条件，领取变得更难，不是更容易。
Only if … will they be eligible 是在限制领取救济金，不是保障领取的权利。

context.text: More apparent reasonableness followed. ==There will now be a seven-day wait for **the jobseeker’s allowance**==. “Those first few days should be spent looking for work, ==not looking to **sign on**==,” he claimed. “We’re doing these things because we know they ==help people **stay off benefits**== and help those on benefits get into work faster.” …

questions.stem: The phrase “to sign on” (Para. 2) most probably means _______.

options.A: to register for an allowance from the government
options.B: to accept the government’s restrictions on the allowance
options.C: to check on the availability of jobs at the jobcentre
options.D: to attend a governmental job-training program

questions.answerZh: 登记领取政府的津贴
basis: 第二段：申请求职者津贴要先等七天；奥斯本说，头几天应该用来找工作，而不是指望 sign on。sign on 和找工作（looking for work）对立，又和上句的求职者津贴（the jobseeker’s allowance）直接相关；下句说这样做是为了帮人们不靠救济金（stay off benefits）。所以 sign on 指登记领取政府的津贴。
map: not looking to sign on / the jobseeker’s allowance
to register for an allowance from the government

wrong.text: 七天等待确实是对津贴的限制，但“接受限制”和“找工作”构不成对立。
到就业中心查看工作机会和找工作是同一方向，而 sign on 是找工作的对立面。
原文没提政府的就业培训项目，它也和求职者津贴联系不上。

context.text: … On first hearing, this was the socially concerned chancellor, trying to change lives for the better, complete with “reforms” to an obviously indulgent system that demands too little effort from the newly unemployed to find work, and subsidises laziness. ==**What motivated him**, we were to understand, was his **zeal** for “fundamental fairness”—**protecting the taxpayer**==, controlling spending and ensuring that only the most deserving claimants received their benefits.

questions.stem: What prompted the chancellor to develop his scheme?

options.A: A desire to secure a better life for all.
options.B: An eagerness to protect the unemployed.
options.C: An urge to be generous to the claimants.
options.D: A passion to ensure fairness for taxpayers.

questions.answerZh: 确保纳税人公平的热情
basis: 第二段末：乍一听（On first hearing），财政大臣是在关心社会、改善民生；但作者提醒我们，真正驱使他的（What motivated him）是对“基本公平”的热情（zeal），也就是保护纳税人、控制开支、确保只有最该得到救济的人才能领到。passion 对应 zeal，ensure fairness for taxpayers 概括了 protecting the taxpayer。
map: zeal for “fundamental fairness”—protecting the taxpayer
A passion to ensure fairness for taxpayers.

wrong.text: 改善所有人的生活是 On first hearing 引出的表象，不是真正的动机。
帮人们不靠救济、尽快就业是奥斯本自己的说法，作者用 Help? Really? 表示怀疑。
新政让申领者更难领到救济金，是更小气，不是更慷慨。

context.text: ==Losing a job is **hurting**==: you don’t skip down to the jobcentre with a song in your heart, delighted at the prospect of doubling your income from the generous state. ==It is **financially terrifying**, **psychologically embarrassing**== and you know that support is minimal and extraordinarily hard to get. ==You are now **not wanted**==; you are now excluded from the work environment that offers purpose and structure in your life. …

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, being unemployed makes one feel _______.

options.C: enraged
options.D: guilty

questions.answerZh: 不安
basis: 第三段：失业令人痛苦（hurting）：经济上让人恐慌（financially terrifying），心理上让人难堪（psychologically embarrassing），救济又少又难领；你不再被需要（not wanted），失去了工作带来的目标和秩序，养家的收入也没了。综合起来，失业让人内心恐慌不安。
map: hurting / financially terrifying / psychologically embarrassing / not wanted
uneasy

wrong.text: hurting 是痛苦，不是受到侮辱。
原文只说救济少、难领，没说失业者感到愤怒。
psychologically embarrassing 指不被需要的难堪，不是内疚。

context.text: … It is as though 20 years of ever-tougher reforms of the job search and benefit administration system never happened. ==The principle of British welfare is **no longer** that== you can insure yourself against the risk of unemployment and ==receive **unconditional payments** if the disaster happens==. Even the very phrase “jobseeker’s allowance” is about redefining the unemployed as a “jobseeker” who had no fundamental right to a benefit he or she has earned through making national insurance contributions. Instead, the claimant receives a time-limited “allowance,” ==**conditional on** actively seeking a job==; no entitlement and no insurance, at £71.70 a week, one of the least generous in the EU.

questions.stem: To which of the following would the author most probably agree?

options.A: Unemployment benefits should not be made conditional.
options.B: The British welfare system indulges jobseekers’ laziness.
options.C: The jobseekers’ allowance has met their actual needs.
options.D: Osborne’s reforms will reduce the risk of unemployment.

questions.answerZh: 失业救济金不应附加条件
basis: 第四段：作者批评新政背离了英国福利制度的原则：过去人们可以为失业投保，失业时得到无条件的救济（unconditional payments），现在却不再如此（no longer），只能拿到有时限、以积极求职为条件（conditional on）的“津贴”，而且是欧盟最低的之一。no longer … Instead 透露出作者对无条件救济的怀念和对设条件的不满，所以作者会同意救济金不应附加条件。
map: no longer … unconditional payments / conditional on
Unemployment benefits should not be made conditional.

wrong.text: 福利制度纵容懒惰是奥斯本的看法，正是作者批驳的对象。
作者说津贴没有保障、是欧盟最低的之一，并不能满足需求。
原文说人们不再能为失业风险投保，不是说改革会降低失业风险。

context.text: … ==The best lawyers made **skyscrapers-full of money**, **tempting** ever more students to pile into law schools==. …

questions.stem: A lot of students take up law as their profession due to _______.

options.C: the prospect of working in big firms
options.D: the attraction of financial rewards

questions.answerZh: 经济回报的吸引力
basis: 第二段：顶尖律师赚的钱多得像摩天大楼（skyscrapers-full of money），吸引着（tempting）越来越多的学生涌进法学院。tempting 前面是原因：律师的高收入。所以学生学法律是被经济回报吸引。
map: made skyscrapers-full of money, tempting
the attraction of financial rewards

wrong.text: 原文只说法律服务支出增速是通胀的两倍，没说客户需求增长是学生学法律的原因。
通胀只是用来比较法律服务支出增速的参照，不是学生学法律的原因。
原文说大多数法学毕业生根本进不了大律所。

context.text: … There is just one path for a lawyer in most American states: ==a four-year undergraduate degree in some **unrelated subject**==, then a three-year law degree at one of 200 law schools authorized by the American Bar Association and an expensive preparation for the bar exam. ==This leaves today’s average law-school graduate with **$100,000 of debt**== on top of undergraduate debts. …

questions.stem: Which of the following adds to the costs of legal education in most American states?

options.A: Higher tuition fees for undergraduate studies.
options.B: Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in another major.
options.C: Admissions approval from the bar association.
options.D: Receiving training by professional associations.

questions.answerZh: 攻读另一专业的学士学位
basis: 第三段：法律教育费用过高。在美国大多数州，当律师只有一条路：先在某个无关专业读四年本科（undergraduate degree in some unrelated subject），再读三年法学学位，还要花大钱准备律师资格考试；结果毕业生平均背上十万美元的债。在另一个专业读学士学位正是其中一项。another major 对应 unrelated subject。
map: a four-year undergraduate degree in some unrelated subject
Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in another major.

wrong.text: 原文提到本科债务，但没比较本科学费的高低。

原文是在美国律师协会认证的法学院读书，不是接受专业协会的培训。

context.text: Reforming the system would help both lawyers and their customers. Sensible ideas have been around for a long time, but ==**the state-level bodies that govern the profession** have been **too conservative** to implement them==. …

questions.stem: Hindrance to the reform of the legal system originates from _______.

options.C: the rigid bodies governing the profession
options.D: the stern exam for would-be lawyers

questions.answerZh: 管理该行业的僵化机构
basis: 第四段：改革制度对律师和客户都有好处。合理的建议早就有了，但州一级管理这个行业的机构（the state-level bodies that govern the profession）太保守（too conservative），不肯实施。改革的阻碍来自这些僵化的管理机构。rigid 对应 too conservative。
map: the state-level bodies that govern the profession have been too conservative
the rigid bodies governing the profession

wrong.text: 非律师人士出现在第五段，说的是所有权结构，原文没说他们批评改革。
原文说改革对律师和客户都有好处，没说他们抵制。
律师资格考试是改革建议（提前参加）涉及的内容，不是改革的阻碍。

context.text: The other reason why costs are so high is the restrictive guild-like ownership structure of the business. Except in the District of Columbia, ==**non-lawyers** may not own any share of a law firm==. This keeps fees high and innovation slow. There is pressure for change from within the profession, but opponents of change among the regulators insist that ==**keeping outsiders out** of a law firm== isolates lawyers from the pressure to make money rather than serve clients ethically.

questions.stem: The guild-like ownership structure is considered “restrictive” partly because it _______.

options.A: prevents lawyers from gaining due profits
options.B: keeps lawyers from holding law-firm shares
options.C: aggravates the ethical situation in the trade
options.D: bans outsiders’ involvement in the profession

questions.answerZh: 禁止外部人员参与该行业
basis: 第五段：费用高的另一个原因是类似行会的限制性所有权结构。除了哥伦比亚特区，非律师（non-lawyers）不能持有律所的任何股份；监管者中的反对者也坚持把外人挡在律所之外（keeping outsiders out）。“限制性”就体现在禁止外人参与这个行业。
map: non-lawyers may not own any share / keeping outsiders out
bans outsiders’ involvement in the profession

wrong.text: 反对者认为这种结构让律师免受挣钱的压力，原文没说它让律师拿不到应有的利润。
不能持股的是非律师，选项换成了律师。
反对者认为这种结构能让律师更有道德地服务客户，没说它让行业道德状况恶化。

==**Reforming the system** would help both lawyers and their customers==. …

questions.stem: In this text, the author mainly discusses _______.

options.A: flawed ownership of America’s law firms and its causes
options.B: the factors that help make a successful lawyer in America
options.C: a problem in America’s legal profession and solutions to it
options.D: the role of undergraduate studies in America’s legal education

questions.answerZh: 美国法律行业的一个问题及其解决方案
basis: 前两段提出问题：美国人对律师抱怨最多，法律服务费用高得像噩梦（costly nightmare）。后面分两层分析原因并给办法：一是法律教育费用太高，可以允许本科学法律、提前考律师资格；二是限制性的所有权结构，可以允许非律师持股，美国应该效仿其他国家（America should follow）。全文讲的是美国法律行业的一个问题及其解决办法。

a problem in America’s legal profession and solutions to it

wrong.text: 律所所有权结构只是第五、六段讲的一个原因。

本科阶段只是第三、四段提到的内容，不是全文中心。

context.text: ==The **US$3-million** Fundamental Physics Prize== is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year’s award in March. questions.stem: The Fundamental Physics Prize is seen as _______.

options.A: a symbol of the entrepreneurs’ wealth
options.B: a possible replacement of the Nobel Prizes
options.C: a handsome reward for researchers
options.D: an example of bankers’ investments

questions.answerZh: 给研究人员的丰厚奖励
basis: 第一段：300 万美元（US$3-million）的基础物理学奖的确是一次有趣的尝试；它远不是唯一的一个，近年来有一系列面向研究人员的丰厚奖项（lucrative awards for researchers）加入了诺贝尔奖的行列。可见基础物理学奖是给研究人员的丰厚奖励。handsome reward 对应 lucrative awards。
map: US$3-million / lucrative awards for researchers
a handsome reward for researchers

wrong.text: 企业家的财富是奖金的来源，原文没说奖项是财富的象征。
原文说新奖项加入了诺贝尔奖的行列，推不出它可能取代诺贝尔奖。
奖金来自互联网企业家的银行账户，是捐资，与银行家投资无关。

context.text: … ==The new awards are an exercise in **self-promotion** for **those behind them**==, say scientists. ==They could **distort** the achievement-based system of peer-review-led research==. …

questions.stem: The critics think that the new awards will most benefit _______.

options.B: the founders of the new awards
options.C: the achievement-based system
options.D: peer-review-led research

questions.answerZh: 新奖项的创立者
basis: 第二段：新闻专题文章引用的几位科学家批评说，新奖项是幕后出资人（those behind them）自我宣传（self-promotion）的手段，还可能扭曲（distort）以同行评审为导向、以成就为基础的科研体系。设奖为的是宣传自己，最大的受益者自然是奖项的创立者。
map: an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them
the founders of the new awards

wrong.text: those behind them 指设奖的人，不是科学家，原文也没说科学家逐利。

context.text: … But the Nobel Foundation’s limit of three recipients per prize, each of whom must still be living, ==has long been outgrown by the **collaborative nature of modern research**==—as will be demonstrated by ==the inevitable row over **who is ignored**== when it comes to acknowledging the discovery of the Higgs boson. …

questions.stem: The discovery of the Higgs boson is a typical case which involves _______.

options.A: the joint effort of modern researchers
options.C: the demonstration of research findings
options.D: legitimate concerns over the new prizes

questions.answerZh: 现代研究者的共同努力
basis: 第四段：诺贝尔基金会规定每个奖项最多三人获奖，而且必须在世，这一限制早已跟不上现代科研的合作性质（collaborative nature of modern research）；破折号后举例：在承认希格斯玻色子的发现时，谁会被遗漏（who is ignored）必然引发争议。这说明希格斯玻色子的发现是现代研究者共同努力的成果。

the joint effort of modern researchers

wrong.text: 争议在于获奖名额不够、谁会被遗漏，不是获奖者的地位。

合理担忧针对新旧奖项的分配，希格斯玻色子的例子说的是诺贝尔奖，不是新奖项。

context.text: … The Nobels were, of course, ==themselves set up by **a very rich individual**== who had decided what he wanted to do with his own money. ==**Time, rather than intention**, has given them **legitimacy**==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, which of the following is true of the Nobels?

options.A: History has never cast doubt on them.
options.B: They are the most representative honor.
options.C: Their legitimacy has long been in dispute.
options.D: Their endurance has done justice to them.

questions.answerZh: 它们的持久性证明了自身的价值
basis: 第四段末：诺贝尔奖当年也是一位很有钱的人用自己的钱设立的（a very rich individual）；是时间，而不是设奖的初衷，赋予了它正统地位（Time … has given them legitimacy）。也就是说，诺贝尔奖延续至今，才体现出它的价值。endurance 对应 Time，has done justice to them 对应 has given them legitimacy。
map: Time, rather than intention, has given them legitimacy
Their endurance has done justice to them.

wrong.text: 第四段就指出诺贝尔奖限制获奖人数早已不合时宜，不能说从未受到质疑。
原文没说诺贝尔奖是最有代表性的荣誉。
段末说时间已经赋予诺贝尔奖正统地位，不是说它的正统性长期有争议。

context.text: The US$3-million Fundamental Physics Prize ==is **indeed an interesting experiment**==, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year’s award in March. …

questions.stem: The author believes that the new awards are _______.

options.A: harmful to the culture of research
options.C: subject to undesirable changes

questions.answerZh: 尽管受到批评，但仍可接受

acceptable despite the criticism

context.text: “The Heart of the Matter,” the just-released report by the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (AAAS), ==**deserves praise**== for affirming the importance of the humanities and social sciences to the prosperity and security of liberal democracy in America. ==**Regrettably, however**==, the report’s failure to address the true nature of the crisis facing liberal education ==may cause **more harm than good**==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, what is the author’s attitude toward the AAAS’s report?

options.C: Contemptuous.
options.D: Tolerant.

questions.answerZh: 批评的
